ASTIS-authored same-prox canonical KL/Fisher integration independently sealed before proof.
Under the source normalized globally C2 Hessian bounds kappa^-1 I<=Hessian V<=I, kappa>=1, and positive measurable eta with measurable y, there exists a measurable unique stationary proximal point p. Let R be the actual quadratic reweighting of volume.tilted(-V), let r be its actual affine standardization about the same p, and gamma=stdGaussian E. Then r is a probability absolutely continuous with respect to gamma, canonical KL is finite, the true smooth residual-potential gradient is in L2(r), and KL(r||gamma).toReal<=half integral norm(gradient rho)^2 dr. E is finite complete real Hilbert/Borel, including rank0; no eta upper bound or caller coherence/density/domain/inequality certificate is assumed.
Exact scope: Authored sufficient same-unique-prox canonical KL<=Fisher/2 leaf for the literal standardized RGO. Exact source normalized C2/Hessian assumptions; all positive eta, actual measurable-family extension incl rank0. Probability/AC/finite KL/scoreL2 and same witness are internally derived. Coherent32/33 actual rho/Z/q/f/r transported by uniqueness, true Gaussian functionLSI42 coefficient2 and actual32 energyquarter. No extra witness/coherence/density/law/desiredbound certificate. GaussianT2/W2/FIRST4.6/fullW12/sampling/both mains/error/work/expectedcost/main/live/PURIFIED remain separate.
theorem standardized_rgo_unique_prox_and_kl_le_fisher
    {E S : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    [MeasurableSpace S] {V : E → ℝ} {κ : ℝ}
    (hκ : 1 ≤ κ) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E, κ⁻¹*‖v‖^2 ≤ fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v v ∧
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v v ≤ ‖v‖^2)
    {eta : S → ℝ} {y : S → E} (heta : Measurable eta) (hy : Measurable y)
    (hpos : ∀ s, 0 < eta s) :
    ∃ p : S → E, Measurable p ∧
      (∀ s, p s+eta s • gradient V (p s)=y s) ∧
      (∀ s z, z+eta s • gradient V z=y s → z=p s) ∧
      let rho := fun s u => V (p s+Real.sqrt (eta s) • u)-V (p s)-
        Real.sqrt (eta s)*inner ℝ (gradient V (p s)) u
      let mu := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
      let R := fun s => mu.tilted (fun x => -‖x-y s‖^2/(2*eta s))
      let r := fun s => (R s).map (fun x => (Real.sqrt (eta s))⁻¹ • (x-p s))
      let gamma := stdGaussian E
      ∀ s, IsProbabilityMeasure (r s) ∧ r s ≪ gamma ∧
        _root_.InformationTheory.klDiv (r s) gamma ≠ ⊤ ∧
        MemLp (gradient (rho s)) 2 (r s) ∧
        (_root_.InformationTheory.klDiv (r s) gamma).toReal ≤
          (1/2 : ℝ)*(∫ u, ‖gradient (rho s) u‖^2 ∂r s)

graph_nodes.reconstructed_theorem:
Let E be any finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space, equipped with its norm and Borel measurable structure; dimension zero is allowed. Let S be any measurable space. Let V : E -> R be twice continuously Frechet differentiable on all of E, and let kappa be a real number with kappa >= 1. Suppose, for every x,v in E, that
  kappa^(-1) ||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
Let eta : S -> R and y : S -> E be measurable, and suppose eta(s) > 0 for every s in S.
Then there exists a measurable p : S -> E such that, for every s,
  p(s) + eta(s) grad V(p(s)) = y(s),
and, for every s and every z in E,
  z + eta(s) grad V(z) = y(s) implies z = p(s).
Using this same p, define
  rho_s(u) = V(p(s) + sqrt(eta(s)) u) - V(p(s))
             - sqrt(eta(s)) <grad V(p(s)), u>,
  mu = Tilt(volume_E, x |-> -V(x)),
  R_s = Tilt(mu, x |-> -||x-y(s)||^2/(2 eta(s))),
  T_s(x) = (sqrt(eta(s)))^(-1) (x-p(s)),
  r_s = (T_s)_# R_s,
  gamma = stdGaussian(E).
Here Tilt is the normalized exponential tilt of the indicated measure by the indicated real potential, and gamma is the canonical centered variance-one Gaussian measure on E. For every s in S, r_s is a probability measure, r_s is absolutely continuous with respect to gamma, its canonical ENNReal KL divergence KL(r_s || gamma) is not infinity, and the actual globally defined gradient grad rho_s belongs to L^2(r_s), including almost-everywhere strong measurability and finiteness of its L^2 seminorm. Moreover,
  toReal(KL(r_s || gamma)) <= (1/2) integral_E ||grad rho_s(u)||^2 dr_s(u),
where the integral is the real Bochner integral of the squared Hilbert norm. The statement imposes no upper bound on eta, and supplies rather than assumes the measurable unique stationary witness p.
